text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific location, character, and severity of your sudden abdominal pain, and tell me if you have a history of gallstones, ulcers, or inflammatory bowel disease.

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesenteric Ischemia. The patient's history of recent acute myocardial infarction places him at high risk for embolic occlusion of the mesenteric arteries, and the classic presentation of periumbilical pain followed by bloody stools is highly specific for this condition. I will not ask further questions; immediate imaging is required to confirm. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CTA.
